name: Infant-type Hemispheric Glioma MET-altered
aliases: Infant-type hemispheric glioma with MET alteration

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Molecular and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Infant-type Hemispheric Glioma MET-altered

criteria.description: Presence of high-grade glioma histopathological features in hemispheric brain tissue of infants
Detection of MET gene alteration (fusion or mutation) by molecular genetic testing
Onset in infancy or early childhood (typically under 2 years of age)
Imaging showing large, unilateral hemispheric mass with infiltrative characteristics

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of high-grade glioma combined with molecular evidence of MET gene alteration in a patient under 2 years of age
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for MET alterations is essential to distinguish from other infant-type gliomas.

searchTerms: rapid onset of focal nerve problems
fast progression of localized brain deficits

pathognomonic.symptomName: Seizures refractory to standard antiepileptic therapy

searchTerms: vomiting and irritability from brain pressure
signs of brain swelling in infants

common.symptomName: Headache in infants (manifested as inconsolable crying)
searchTerms: persistent crying due to head pain
reduced muscle tone on one side

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction secondary to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction caused by brain lesion
fluid buildup in brain needing shunting
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

laboratory: CSF analysis typically non-specific; may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI showing large, unilateral hemispheric mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Perilesional edema and mass effect with midline shift
genetic: Presence of MET gene fusion or activating mutation confirmed by next-generation sequencing or FISH
Absence of other common infant glioma alterations such as NTRK or ALK fusions
other: Histopathology demonstrating high-grade glioma features with mitotic activity, necrosis, and microvascular proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of NTRK gene fusion instead of MET alteration
Similar histology but different molecular driver
Tumor located in the pons rather than cerebral hemispheres
Distinct clinical presentation with cranial nerve deficits
Systemic signs of infection and positive viral studies

redFlags: Seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
Signs of increased intracranial pressure with bulging fontanelle
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
Mackay A et al. Molecular profiling of infant-type hemispheric gliomas. Nat Commun. 2021
